newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg tops magazine's European deal table.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg tops magazine's European deal table.

text.p: SBC Warburg, the investment banking arm of Swiss Bank Corp, on Wednesday topped the table of advisers on European cross-border mergers and acquisitions.
The league table, covering the first half of 1997, was compiled by industry magazine Acquisitions Monthly. SBC Warburg rose from seventh position in the overall rankings for 1996.

"The European M&A market continues to be hugely competitive. U.S. banks are making their mark on the marketplace, but European and UK banks are still strong players," the magazine's editor Philip Healey said in a statement.

U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley ranked second in the table, maintaining its position but only fractionally ahead of Swiss banking heavyweight UBS, which showed the greatest improvement by rising from 18th to third.

SBC Warburg advised on 18 deals worth a combined 6.9 billion pounds ($11.2 billion), Morgan Stanley advised on 19 deals worth 5.4 billion pounds and UBS was advisor on 14 deals valued at 5.38 billion pounds.
SBC Warburg's largest deal was the 2.0 billion pound acquisition of the outstanding 43 percent of French pharmaceutical company Roussel Uclaf by German chemicals giant Hoechst AG.
It advised the French company in what was the largest cross-border acquisition in Europe completed during the first half of the year.
It also advised Swiss chemicals firm Clariant on its 1.8 billion pound merger with Hoechst's speciality chemicals arm.

Acquisitions Monthly said activity in the British utilities market continued to play a major part in the make up of the table. Morgan Stanley and UBS advised Entergy Corp on its 1.2 billion pound acquisition of London Electricity Plc.

Smaller British banks were well represented in the top-10 places. Schroders was fifth, advising on 12 deals totalling four billion pounds. The Lazard group ranked sixth and the Rothschild group seventh.
Among the U.S. giants, J.P. Morgan ranked fourth, Goldman Sachs eighth, Merrill Lynch ninth. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was in 10th position. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
